notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null, and no hardware or live ROS run was made. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: reason_code family:ros and helper RosDriver came from a name scan; the confirmed entry symbols are Python Gymnasium environments, so this package uses GymnasiumDriver and the cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 classes. It covers one concrete environment, UR5TaskSpaceEnv-v0 (ur_openai.task_envs.ur5_task_space:UR5TaskSpaceEnv at ur5_task_space.py:17); the other card entry symbols (UR5JointSpaceEnv, UR5GraspEnv, UR5PickAndPlaceEnv and UR5PickAndPlaceRealEnv) are not covered by this one-device package. UR5JointSpaceEnv was not selected because its step falls through to the base _is_terminated while the subclass defines only _is_done (ur5_joint_space.py:203-212 and robot_env.py:75). The upstream ROS/Gazebo environment was not run: its dependencies (ROS Noetic, Gazebo, ur_control, ur_gazebo, ur_pykdl and a catkin workspace) are not installed where the gate ran, and the implicit gym.make('UR5TaskSpaceEnv-v0') sim backend was not exercised. The checked backend is the package's pure Python analytic stand-in (fake.py): it applies the cited 0.001 m per unit action translation and the cited reward, termination and truncation rules, but models no inverse kinematics, joint limits, dynamics, contacts, collisions, grasping, Gazebo physics or ROS graph; it uses placeholder start pose, joint angles, orientation and target jitter. The fake's observation is the same 32-element upstream concatenation (6 joint angles + 7 end-effector pose + 7 target pose + 6 pose error + 6 velocity); the size is not reduced. The action space is the cited upstream Box(-1., 1.) with 3 values (task_space.yaml:28). The runtime latch refuses further step/reset calls after an e-stop but cannot interrupt one in-flight native env.step; no physical stop is present or claimed. Warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only stores the seed for the next reset and makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived seed, ticks and action.values inputs; G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue_requests. check-report.json was regenerated by the gate and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the GymnasiumDriver deviation, action_space_ref (ur5_task_space.py:38-40), all 19 facts, the fake's delta translation (action * 0.001 m, as upstream) and the stop text against ur5_task_space.py, robot_env.py, ur5_env.py, gazebo_connection.py and ur_control at the pin. The safe_state said the simulation stops advancing, but get_robot_params leaves param_use_gazebo False for every driver value (ur5_task_space.py:74-81), so UR5TaskSpaceEnv always uses the no-op RobotConnection (gazebo_connection.py:22-33), never pauses Gazebo, and its Arm commands scaled_pos_joint_traj_controller, the controller name that ur_gazebo and the real UR driver share; three facts also said more than their lines (the step fact omitted the _pause_env branch, the _reset_sim fact dropped the second unpause and check, the set_target_pose_flex fact claimed a rate period that is on line 48). Reviewer changed driver.py (docstring, safe_state, the three facts, 18 new source facts on the no-op connection, the shared controller name, sys.exit() on a NaN action, the input() block after a ur3/pause message, rospy.signal_shutdown on close, the /home/imr sys.path entry, ignored IK_NOT_FOUND and SPEED_LIMIT_EXCEEDED returns, the curriculum threshold and UR5PickAndPlaceRealEnv, and four fidelity gaps) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL (seed stored for the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT warnings and the digest unchanged; the author's notes on the stop and the step, now stale, stay as written. For the human reviewer: Fake-only contract; no sim backend is declared, and the implicit gym.make('UR5TaskSpaceEnv-v0') route needs the upstream register_environment call. Upstream UR5TaskSpaceEnv cannot tell Gazebo from a real arm: it never pauses Gazebo (RobotConnection does nothing) and publishes JointTrajectory commands to scaled_pos_joint_traj_controller, which the real UR ROS driver also serves, so constructed against a real driver it moves a real UR5 (an arm, R2 or above) with no acknowledged stop; the software latch only refuses new steps while the trajectory controller holds the last target. Live construction in the server process would read ur_gym/driver without a default, prepend /home/imr paths to sys.path, call sys.exit() on a NaN action, block on input() after a ur3/pause message and call rospy.signal_shutdown on close. UR5PickAndPlaceRealEnv (driver: robot, gripper state on /ur_hardware_interface/tool_data) is a real-robot environment and is not covered.

MODEL REVIEW (grok-4.7, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Item 12 repair. Arm publishes JointTrajectory on <ns>/scaled_pos_joint_traj_controller/command (arm.py:115-127; constants.py:4). ur5_controllers.yaml:5-25 defines that controller as position_controllers/JointTrajectoryController on the six UR joints. get_robot_params leaves param_use_gazebo False for every driver value (ur5_task_space.py:74-81), so the class commands the controller name the real UR driver also uses. No fact cites that only Gazebo consumes the topic, so the class risk is R2, an arm. safe_state and facts.md say the latch sends no zero trajectory and does not stop a UR arm on that controller. The reference was regenerated. python3 -m mhs.driver check --backend fake passed with the same stable digest sha256:cbb775f9eefd2fe0f1b554852a082c5f300be019d286ae677208275442fb9267, and G9 passed. Evidence is contract_checked on the fake only. reviewed_by stays null.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Different-model review by Codex (gpt-6.1-sol) of the work of Grok (grok-4.7), unit p5-backlog-packages--bl04, round 1: Verified the trajectory publisher, controller name and get_robot_params behavior. R2 is justified, and the revised description accurately discloses continued target holding without a native stop. Strict collection passed. For the human reviewer: A live UR arm requires separately validated stopping and recovery.
